You build mogrts files, component libraries, and motion guidelines that other people can use independently, and every project is an opportunity to make the next one ship faster</p> </li> <li> <p>You understand brand as well as UI: timing, easing, personality, the emotional register that makes motion feel ownable rather than generic</p> </li> <li> <p>You have a strong sense of sound and rhythm. proactively so stakeholders understand the why behind every creative choice</p> </li> <li> <p>You use AI as a genuine part of your practice, experimenting with video tools and sharing what you figure out so the whole team benefits</p> </li> <li> <p>You're energized by ambiguity, move fast, and don't wait for perfect conditions</p> <p>&nbsp;</p> </li> </ul> <p><strong>Things You’ll Do:</strong></p> storyboards yourself for straightforward projects so we can move fast without a separate brief-to-board cycle</p> </li> <li> <p>Work directly from UI frames provided by the product team to build polished product demo animations and feature explainers</p> </li> <li> <p>Build Zapier's motion design language: ownable branded motion patterns that establish how Zapier feels in motion across every surface</p> </li> <li> <p>Create motion guidelines, component libraries, and mogrts files that give partners and social teams repeatable building blocks to work from independently</p> </li> <li> paid social testing across multiple angles and formats</p> </li> <li> <p>Support the recurring product video format and turn it into a scalable template for future launches</p> </li> </ul> <p>&nbsp;</p> <h2><strong>How to Apply</strong></h2> <p>At Zapier, we believe that diverse perspectives and experiences make us better, which is why we have a non-standard application process designed All we ask is that you answer a few in-depth questions in our application that would typically be asked at the start of an interview process. This helps speed things up by letting us get to know you and your skillset a bit better right out of the gate. Please be sure to answer each question; the resume and CV fields are optional.</p> <p>Education is not a requirement for our roles; however, if you receive an offer, you will need to include your most recent educational experience as part of our background check process.</p> <p>After you apply, you are going to hear back from us—even if we don’t see an immediate fit with our team. We know we’ll make mistakes from time to time, so if you ever have questions about where you stand or about the process, just ask your recruiter!</p> <p>Zapier is an equal-opportunity employer and we're excited to work with talented and empathetic people of all identities. Zapier does not discriminate based on someone's identity in any aspect of hiring or employment as required by law and in line with our commitment to Diversity, Inclusion, Belonging and Equity. oldContent: MarkTechPost https://www.marktechpost.com/ An Artificial Intelligence News Platform Thu, 15 Oct 2026 19:53:52 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=7.1.3 https://www.marktechpost.com/wp-content/uploads/2022/04/cropped-Favicon-512-x-512-1-1-32x32.png MarkTechPost https://www.marktechpost.com/ 32 32 127842392 NVIDIA Releases Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B Open Multimodal Agent Model https://www.marktechpost.com/2026/10/15/nvidia-nemotron-3-5-super-vl-release/ Thu, 15 Oct 2026 19:53:50 +0000 https://www.marktechpost.com/?p=82957 NVIDIA released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, an open 120B-parameter multimodal MoE model with 12B active parameters, 1M-token context and NVFP4 weights that run on 1 DGX Spark, plus 2 Bolt edge models. The post NVIDIA Releases Nemotron 3.5 Super VL, a 120B Open Multimodal Agent Model appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> NVIDIA just released Nemotron 3.5 Super VL , an open vision-language model built for always-on enterprise agents. Nemotron 3.5 Super VL is a 120B-parameter mixture-of-experts model from NVIDIA that activates 12B parameters per token. It reads text, images, documents and video, then reasons, calls tools and writes code in one model. For developers, 1 open checkpoint replaces a separate text model along with a separate vision model. NVIDIA also shipped 2 edge models, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B and Bolt E4B. TL;DR Size: 120B total parameters, 12B active (MoE). Context up to 1M tokens. Runs on: 1x DGX Spark, 1x H200, 2x H100 or 1x GB200 with the NVFP4 checkpoint. A BF16 checkpoint is also published. Performance: Strong reasoning, agentic coding and document vision. NVIDIA claims up to 5x higher single-GPU throughput than open peers. Best: 89.90 on GPQA-Diamond (NVFP4). Worst: 17.78 on tau3-bench banking (NVFP4). What is Nemotron 3.5 Super VL? It is an open multimodal agent model. Weights ship under the OpenMDW-1.1 license . NVIDIA also released open datasets , training recipes and RL environments in NeMo Gym. The model card lists text, image and video inputs with text output. Video is limited to MP4 clips up to 2 minutes. Reasoning can be toggled on or off through the chat template. How does the architecture work? The backbone interleaves Mamba-2, mixture-of-experts and attention layers. Each MoE layer holds 512 routed experts. A C-RADIO vision encoder and a connector feed images, document pages and video frames into the language backbone. Speed comes from four techniques: Multi-token prediction: a native drafter proposes several tokens, verified in 1 forward pass. LiLiCorr: a speculative drafter for DGX Spark, up to 2.3x faster token generation. NVFP4 with quantization-aware distillation: 4-bit weights and activations on Blackwell, 4-bit weights with 16-bit activations elsewhere. Context reuse: prefix caching keeps both attention caches and Mamba states across agent turns. The model was distilled from Nemotron 3 Ultra. NVIDIA team states that it trained on about 26 trillion tokens. Post-training used roughly 3.8 million samples plus RL across dozens of environments. Continued pretraining added 10B Indic tokens. How does it perform on benchmarks? All scores below are NVIDIA-reported, from the NVFP4 checkpoint on the model card. Area Benchmark Score Reasoning GPQA-Diamond 89.90 Coding SWE-bench Verified 71.07 Coding Terminal-Bench 2.1 60.80 Web agent BrowseComp 77.5 Instruction following IFBench 71.50 Charts CharXiv reasoning 79.88 Documents MMLongBench-Doc 62.82 Computer use OSWorld-Verified 52.3 Long-horizon agent tau3-bench banking 17.78 On agent harness evals, Super VL beats Nemotron 3 Ultra. It scores 63.44% on Hermes Bench versus 56.33%. On LangChain evals it scores 87.05% versus 84.3%. Ultra carries about 4.6x more total parameters. NVIDIA team reports over 600 output tokens per second on Artificial Analysis agentic tasks via a Baseten endpoint. It scores 65 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index and costs $0.042 per million input tokens. The post Liquid AI Releases d1-ultra: A Multimodal Decision Model That Scores 65 on the AA Decision Index appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> Liquid AI has released d1-ultra , its most capable decision model to date. The Liquid AI d1-ultra decision model reads text, images, or both. It answers typed questions with a probability for each possible answer. It does this in one forward pass and generates no output tokens. For developers, that means classification, routing and scoring calls without paying for generated text. It is available now on the Liquid API at $0.042 per million input tokens. TL;DR Size: Parameters and context length not disclosed. Built on a larger open-weight backbone than d1. Runs on: Hosted Liquid API only. No downloadable weights or quantized variants announced. Performance: Leads all 8 categories in Liquid’s 112-evaluation suite, per Liquid. Best: 65 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index, ranked #1 (Liquid-reported). Worst: No public per-benchmark breakdown or parameter count yet; claims are vendor-reported. What is a decision model? A decision model answers bounded questions with probabilities instead of free text. Liquid’s decision model docs describe 3 question types: Noul: a yes/no question that returns a probability between 0 and 1. Choice: one label from a set, with a probability per label. Score: a probability-weighted position on an ordered rubric. The docs recommend decision models for routing, moderation, guardrails, triage and LLM-as-judge replacement. They recommend a language model for summarization, chat and code generation. How does d1-ultra work? Each request carries a state (the context), optional images , and 1 or more typed questions . The model evaluates every question against the same input in 1 call. The d1 API reference shows responses with output_tokens always at 0. Liquid AI team states that d1-ultra uses a larger open-weight backbone than d1 , along with heavy Liquid-specific customizations. Combined with Liquid’s decision training pipeline, the gains are largest on knowledge tasks. Liquid AI team built d1-ultra for messy cases. Its examples include spotting a circuit board defect against a spec. Another is checking a damage claim against the customer’s photo. How does d1-ultra perform on benchmarks? Liquid AI compared d1-ultra against its earlier d1 and TypeSafe’s Jev 1.14 across 112 evaluations. According to Liquid AI’s announcement , d1-ultra outperforms Jev 1.14 across all tasks at the same price. On the independent Artificial Analysis Decision Index , Liquid reports d1-ultra ranks #1 with a score of 65. The index averages 4 evaluations at 25% each: AA-Omniscience-Decision: knowledge and hallucination HLE-MultiChoice: reasoning When2Call: tool calling WildGuardTest: safety classification For context, Artificial Analysis’s Oct 13 launch article listed Jev 1.13 first at 58. GLiDE and Microsoft-Decision-1 followed at 54 each. Comparison: d1-ultra vs other decision models Feature d1-ultra d1 Jev (TypeSafe) Microsoft-Decision-1 GLiDE (Fastino) Developer Liquid AI Liquid AI TypeSafe AI Microsoft Fastino Labs Parameters Not disclosed Not disclosed Not disclosed Not disclosed Not disclosed Input Text, images Text, images Text Not disclosed Not disclosed Weights API only API only Closed Not disclosed Not disclosed AA Decision Index 65 (Liquid-reported) Not disclosed 58 (v1.13, Oct 13) 54 (Oct 13) 54 (Oct 13) Price $0.042 / 1M input Not disclosed $0.042 / 1M input $31 / 1M tasks (AA) $119 / 1M tasks (AA) Output tokens billed No No No Not disclosed Not disclosed How do you deploy d1-ultra, and what does it cost? d1-ultra runs on the Liquid API through the /decisions/v1/systemone endpoint with "model": "d1-ultra" . Liquid says Vercel AI Gateway and OpenRouter support is coming soon. You can test it first in the d1 Playground . Billing covers input tokens only. Per Liquid’s pricing notes , images cost 1.5 tokens per 32×32-pixel patch. A 1024×1024 image therefore costs 1,536 tokens. Each question is billed as its own prompt, including its text and all images. So 3 questions on 1 image bill that image 3 times. The endpoint docs cap requests at 8 images and 10,000 image patches. The full JSON body must stay under 4.5 MB. Key Takeaways d1-ultra returns probabilities for text and image decisions with 0 output tokens. Liquid reports a #1 score of 65 on the Artificial Analysis Decision Index. It costs $0.042 per 1M input tokens, the same rate as TypeSafe’s Jev. Liquid claims the lowest calibration error in its tests, useful for routing thresholds. Size, backbone and weights remain undisclosed; access is API-only. Check out the official blog post , the decision model docs , and try the d1 Playground . All credit goes to the researcher of this project. The post Meta Releases Muse Spark Open: 816B Open-Weight MoE With 1M Context appeared first on MarkTechPost . ]]> Meta Superintelligence Labs has released Muse Spark Open , the open-weight version of its Muse Spark model. Muse Spark Open is an 816B-parameter Mixture-of-Experts model that activates 42B parameters per token. It takes text, image, video and audio input, returns text, and holds a 1M-token context window. Meta team claims it to be the most capable US open-weight model to date. For developers, the real news is deployment: the NVFP4 build runs on 2 Apple M5 Ultra Mac Studios. TL;DR Size: 816B total / 42B active parameters (256 experts, 8 active per token); 1M-token context. Runs on: 2 Mac Studios (M5 Ultra, 512 GB each) via MLX; 4 Blackwell Ultra GPUs or 8 H200s with NVFP4; about 300 GB setups via Unsloth 2-bit GGUF. Performance: Strong on agentic tool use; mid-pack among large open models on coding. Best: MCP-Atlas 89.2, the top score in Meta’s comparison table. Worst: Terminal-Bench 2.1 76.4, behind Kimi K3 (85.0), GLM 5.3 (83.9) and Qwen3.8 (82.0). What is Muse Spark Open? Muse Spark Open is a natively multimodal MoE model from Meta, built for coding and long-horizon agentic work. Weights ship in BF16 and NVFP4 on Hugging Face. The open version received extra safety post-training. Meta team states that this makes it more robust without system-level guardrails. How does the architecture work? The model card lists 62 layers and a hidden dimension of 8192. Each MoE layer holds 256 experts, and top-k routing activates 8 per token. Attention is grouped-query, with 128 query heads and 16 KV h

Might you roll your eyes and dismiss their comments as naivety? Or would you indulge their curiosity? As AI has made knowledge accessible on a scale never seen before, companies are becoming leaner and operating faster. What once took a large team months to do can now be done by a handful of people in a few days. It is undeniable that autonomous systems are changing the way we work. In the small and dynamic teams of the future, choosing the right humans to direct your AI systems will become make or break for a company. As a six-time founder, I’ve learned the best workplaces are the ones where questioning things is the norm. Here’s how to build a team that questions orders as much as it obeys them. AI by design Eric Francia, co-founder and CEO of Uniplay. “AI by design” doesn’t only mean building the right autonomous systems. It’s also about creating autonomous humans. You need to trust the human in the loop as much as you do the technology. The team around you ultimately shapes the company in ways you can’t control. So surrounding yourself with people you trust to make decisions when you’re not in the room is critical to success. The nature of job roles is changing. A job description can be totally different from the one advertised by the time you’ve found a candidate, and a six-month roadmap is outdated by the time you’ve finished drawing it up. The World Economic Forum has stated that 59% of employees will need to reskill by 2030 as AI reshapes the workplace. Hiring for a fixed set of skills won’t move the needle. The people worth investing in are those who are able to learn what comes next. Hire for curiosity Curiosity is the best trait you can hire for. When I look at a CV, it’s not just experience or academic credentials that draw me in. I look for what people have built on the side. What have they made on their own initiative? Hire for curiosity, and you’ll create an environment where people are willing to throw new ideas around and challenge outdated ways of doing things. If your team is worried about saying the wrong thing, they won’t end up saying the right thing either. In a world where technology is turning everything on its head, the companies that will thrive are the ones with curious people who are able to adapt to change quickly. Hand over real responsibility Employees with autonomy operate faster. They make better decisions because company vision is not abstract to people who are given real responsibility to drive it. Being involved in strategic direction stitches an employee into the fabric of the company and keeps them engaged. Trust your employees to know what isn’t working. Allow people to pursue new ideas and reinvent things. Your employees are likely to spot potential problems before you do when they’re closer to the product. Make sure your team has the autonomy to try to fix them before they take hold. Boredom is a big business risk As companies become smaller, employee retention is more important than ever. Losing your best people is costlier when you have fewer of them to begin with. The effects of a bored employee surface quickly in a small team. Boredom makes talented people a little bit slower, and a lot less likely to try the difficult thing. The challenge for modern leaders is keeping your team engaged and interested. A bored employee is more likely to be swayed by a flattering LinkedIn recruiter. Make sure to invest in development, keep your team learning, and always encourage curiosity. Give people autonomy and responsibility from the beginning, and boredom has nowhere to take hold. The mentality of risk and the drive to challenge something outdated is what you need to succeed in the changing work environment. Dare to be a beginner, and teach your team to do the same. That junior employee questioning how you’ve always done things could be the most valuable person in the room. Eric Francia is co-founder and CEO of Stockholm-based Uniplay , an agent-driven, game-based learning platform. He has experience building, exiting and scaling digital companies across 70 countries. Uniplay is his sixth company to date. newContent: Crunchbase News https://news.crunchbase.com/ Data-driven reporting on private markets, startups, founders, and investors Thu, 15 Oct 2026 17:19:55 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=6.8.11 https://news.crunchbase.com/wp-content/uploads/cb_news_favicon-150x150.png Crunchbase News https://news.crunchbase.com/ 32 32 Asia’s Startup Funding At Near Record High In Q3, Driven By AI https://news.crunchbase.com/venture/q3-2026-asia-startup-funding-near-record-ai/ Fri, 16 Oct 2026 11:00:42 +0000 https://news.crunchbase.com/?p=94235 Asia’s startup funding held up at the second-highest level in years in the third quarter, even as investment fell slightly from Q2 totals. Overall, investors put $38.5 billion into reported seed- through growth-stage financings for countries in the region in Q3, per Crunchbase data. Of that, a majority went to AI-focused companies, echoing the trends we’ve seen globally . Deal counts, meanwhile, were relatively flat. That indicates concentration of capital into favored startups remains pronounced but is not intensifying. Table of contents An AI-driven quarter China leads by far in country-by-country breakdown Late stage Early stage Seed A big quarter for China Methodology Glossary of funding terms An AI-driven quarter Around 55% of investment — an estimated $21 billion — went to AI-focused companies. Total funding is down substantially from the prior quarter, which was boosted by a $7.4 billion financing for China’s DeepSeek , but still the second-highest tally on record. For Q3, a couple of extra-large rounds bolstered the AI investment tally. The largest went to Beijing-based foundational model company Moonshot AI , which secured $3.5 billion in July at a reported $35 billion valuation. Kling AI , the AI spinout of China-based short video platform Kuaishou Technology , was the second-biggest fundraiser. The generative video startup raised around $3 billion in a July financing that included Baidu and Tencent . China leads by far in country-by-country breakdown China was the leading Asian destination for venture investment by a very wide margin. Per Crunchbase data, roughly $27 billion — or 70% of all Asian startup funding in Q3 — went to China-based companies. India was a distant second, with $2.9 billion, followed by Singapore, with $2.5 billion. For perspective, below we charted third-quarter startup funding tallies for the six countries with the largest totals. Late stage Most capital went to late- and growth-stage funding rounds. Per Crunchbase data, investment at this stage totaled around $20 billion in Q3. That’s down a bit from the prior quarter but nearly double year-ago levels and the second-strongest showing in four years. Multiple jumbo rounds kept the total high. The largest was Moonshot AI’s aforementioned $3.5 billion Series F. Several others raised financings in the multiple hundreds of millions. Shenzhen-based D-Robotics , a provider of robotics hardware and software, for instance, picked up $400 million in a September Series C. And Hong Kong-based Qupital , an e-commerce fintech platform, secured $300 million in Series C funding as it eyes an IPO. Early stage Early-stage investment drifted lower in Q3 but remained at historically high levels. Per Crunchbase data, financing for startups at the Series A and Series B stages totaled $13.6 billion for the just-ended quarter. That’s a decline of 28% from the prior quarter but up 65% from year-ago levels. Seed Reported seed funding hit its highest level in years, boosted by investor enthusiasm around AI. In total, investors poured $4.9 billion into reported seed and angel deals across Asia, per Crunchbase data. That’s up around 22% from the prior quarter and more than double year-ago levels. A big quarter for China Overall, Q3 was a robust period for venture funding to China-based companies, with far smaller sums going to other Asian startup hubs. Funding to startups based in India and Singapore was down significantly quarter over quarter, while Israel’s investment totals declined slightly. We’ll keep an eye out in the coming months to see if this divergence of fortunes persists. US$1,000 per task, and you can do as many tasks as you want.</p> <p>You turn a real change from a repository you know into a task that today's best AI coding models struggle with: hard for the models, but fair for a skilled engineer. Your tasks are used to measure and train AI coding models.</p> <p>Remote, any location. US$1,000 per task that passes review. Minimum of one task a week, about 10 hours a week.</p> <p><strong>How it works</strong></p> <ol class="iiilu2 iiil4m iiimkb"> <li><strong>Apply. </strong>Complete a short screener interview and upload your resume.</li> <li><strong>Propose.</strong> Once you're selected, pick a change from a repository you know and submit a short proposal. We approve it or suggest a better candidate.</li> <li><strong>Build.</strong> In our platform, set up the repository as it was before the change, then write the brief, the correct solution and the grading checks.</li> <li><strong>Stress-test. </strong>Try lazy, incorrect and shortcut solutions and make sure your checks catch them.</li> <li><strong>Model testing.</strong> Run your task against leading AI models until strong models often fail but a skilled engineer can clearly solve it.</li> <li><strong>Review.</strong> A reviewer checks your task and you revise it. Most tasks take more than one round.</li> <li><strong>Next task.</strong> Once your task is accepted, start another.</li> </ol> <p><strong>Requirements</strong></p> <ul class="iiilu2 iiil4n iiimkb"> <li>2+ years of professional software engineering</li> <li>Code merged into a public open-source repository, ideally one you know well. A private codebase you own may also qualify (not employer or client code)</li> <li>Strong in at least one of Python, TypeScript, Go, Rust, Java or C++</li> <li>Solid with Docker, Linux, Git and automated testing</li> <li>Regular use of an AI coding tool</li> <li>Experience writing tests, rubrics or evaluation criteria, ideally for AI models</li> <li>You can explain a change clearly and concisely, in your own words</li> <li>At least 10 hours a week, starting now</li> <li>A secure personal or work computer (no public or shared machines)</li> </ul> <p><strong>Nice to have</strong></p> <ul class="iiilu2 iiil4n iiimkb"> <li>Deep expertise in one area, such as databases, compilers, distributed systems, security or infrastructure</li> <li>Experience building agent tasks or RL environments</li> </ul> <p><strong>Terms</strong></p> <ul class="iiilu2 iiil4n iiimkb"> <li>US$1,000 for each task that passes our quality review, paid directly to you</li> <li>Once your proposal is qualified, you sign Askable's contract and accept its terms</li> <li>The work is used for AI training. Notable customers include Chipotle, Cloudflare, Docusign, Fox, Nvidia, Salesforce, Spotify, Zoom and more. We are growing rapidly and hiring top talent with leading AI skills across engineering, sales, product, marketing, and beyond as we build the leading digital operations platform.</p> <p>&nbsp;</p></div><p class="first-token"><span class="">We are seeking a technical and customer-focused <strong>Solutions Consultant</strong> to join our team</span><span class="">. They will run the technical discovery process and provide guidance, relationship-building, and support throughout the sales process to ensure customer success</span><span class="">. </span></p> <p class="first-token"><span>As a Solutions Consultant at PagerDuty, you’ll sit at the nexus between pre-sales, sales, and customer experience and success</span><span>. capabilities</span><span>.</span></p> <h3>Key responsibilities</h3> <ul> <li><span>Actively identify potential roadblocks and provide thoughtful, technical solutions</span></li> <li><span>Run technical discovery processes to understand customer environments and potential technical landmines</span></li> <li><span>Design integrations to provide seamless implementation with the customer's current technology stack</span></li> <li><span>Support sales cycles by handling technical questions in RFPs, RFIs, and security questionnaires</span></li> <li><span>Break down complex technical concepts and clearly articulate PagerDuty's business value to stakeholders from DevOps engineers up to C-level executives</span></li> <li><span>Support one of our over 375+ native integrations to help customers realize and optimize PagerDuty's capabilities</span></li> <li><span>Partner with sales, product, and cross-functional teams with a focus on growth and exceptional customer service</span></li> <li><span>Manage multiple tasks independently and collaboratively using project management and account management skills</span></li> <li><span>Come up to speed quickly, learn continuously, and apply impeccable attention to detail to all tasks</span></li> </ul> <h3>Basic qualifications</h3> <ul> <li><span>5+ years of pre-sales experience</span></li> <li><span>Bachelor's degree or higher, preferably in a technical field</span></li> <li><span>Ability to do basic scripting (Java, PHP, Ruby, Perl) and a fundamental knowledge of Linux</span></li> <li><span>Experience selling SaaS in a fierce environment</span></li> <li><span>Strong communication skills to build and manage relationships with new and existing clients, with a focus on growth</span></li> <li><span>Demonstrable knowledge of IT monitoring tools or IT Operations</span></li> <li><span>Excellent at multi-tasking, self-driven, and able to work both independently and with cross-functional teams</span></li> <li><span>Ability to travel to customer sites as necessary</span></li> </ul> <h3>Preferred qualifications</h3> <ul> <li><span>Understanding of monitoring systems such as New Relic, Nagios, Zenoss, Splunk, ServiceNow, and Zabbix</span></li> <li><span>Familiarity and knowledge of PagerDuty's space, or already being a fan of our product</span></li> <li><span>Experience in both enterprise and commercial sales</span></li> </ul> <p>PagerDuty is a flexible, hybrid workplace. We embrace and encourage in-person working as an integral part of our culture. Both our employees and external research tells us that co-located collaboration strengthens connections, drives innovation, and accelerates learning.</p> <p>The base salary range for this position is 144,000 - 197,200 USD. This role may also be eligible for bonus, commission, equity, and/or benefits.</p> <p>Our base salary ranges are determined by role, level, and location. The range, which is subject to change based on primary work location, reflects the minimum and maximum base salary we expect to pay newly hired employees for the position. Within the range, we determine pay for an individual based on a number of factors including market location, job-related knowledge, skills/competencies and experience.</p> <p>Your recruiter can share more about the specific offerings for this role, as well as the salary range for your primary work location during the hiring process.</p><div class="content-conclusion"><p><strong>Hesitant to apply?</strong></p> <p>We encourage you to submit your resume even if you don't meet every requirement. If this just isn’t the right role or time - sign up for <a href="https://careers.pagerduty.com/jobalerts">job alerts</a>!</p> <p><strong>Where we work</strong></p> <p>PagerDuty operates a hybrid work model with <a href="https://careers.pagerduty.com/locations">offices</a> in 8 major cities: Atlanta, Lisbon, London, San Francisco, Santiago, Sydney, Tokyo, and Toronto. newContent: We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more https://weworkremotely.com/remote-jobs.rss We Work Remotely: Remote jobs in design, programming, marketing and more en-US 60 Sanctuary Computer: Head of Technology Anywhere in the World New York Full-Stack Programming Full-Time <img src="https://we-work-remotely.imgix.net/logos/0171/3386/logo.gif?ixlib=rails-4.0.0&w=50&h=50&dpr=2&fit=fill&auto=compress" /> <p> <strong>Headquarters:</strong> New York City <br /><strong>URL:</strong> <a href="https://sanctuary.computer">https://sanctuary.computer</a> </p> <p>We are hiring a <strong>Head of Technology</strong> for the garden3d creative collective, to lead engineering at Sanctuary Computer and garden3d in the era of agentic computer code.</p> <p><a href="https://garden3d.notion.site/Head-of-Technology-3f9131fea2c7815da5e3ec914835c397?source=copy_link"><strong>Original job posting link</strong></a></p> <h3><strong>About <a href="https://garden3d.net/">garden3d</a></strong></h3> <p>We are worker owned creative collective, innovating on everything from brands and IRL communities to IoT devices and cross platform apps. We share profit, open source everything, spin out new businesses, and invest in exciting ideas through financial and/or in-kind contributions.</p> <p>Our client roster includes Google, Stripe, Figma, Hinge, Black Socialists in America, ACLU, Pratt, Parsons, Mozilla, The Nobel Prize, MIT, Gnosis, Etsy &amp; Gagosian.</p> <p>We’re the software team behind innovative products like The Light Phone &amp; Mill, and we operate a global, decentralized community space collective called Index Space.</p> <p>We think of our garden3d as collective for creative people, prioritizing a happy, talented, and diverse studio culture. We work on projects that bring value to our world, and we balance deep care for the work we do with a genuine curiosity about life outside of our jobs.</p> <h3><strong>Sanctuary Computer - Development</strong></h3> <p>At <strong><a href="https://www.sanctuary.computer/">Sanctuary Computer</a></strong> we’re building a different type of technology shop – one that prioritizes close collaboration between the client and the craftsperson.</p> <p>Our projects range from design-forward websites, to robust web apps, to native mobile development.</p> <h3><strong>XXIX - Design</strong></h3> <p>When we started <strong><a href="https://www.xxix.co/">XXIX</a></strong> in 2013, we set out to create a different kind of design studio and we’ve thrived because we continually ask what a creative practice can be.</p> <p>We’re building a radically different kind of organization that values autonomy, growth, transparency, and shared responsibility.</p> <h3><strong>Index - Community</strong></h3> <p><strong><a href="https://www.index-space.org/">Index</a></strong> is network of physical spaces all around the world, Index provides space for the exchange of knowledge and tools.</p> <p>We nurture trust within the creative community through generosity and abundance of ideas and care.</p> <h3><strong><a href="https://feed.garden3d.net/">garden3d TK</a> — Media</strong></h3> <p>At garden3d, we’re in the early stages of building an experimental media company exploring emerging themes related to the evolving landscape of technology, design and culture.</p> <p>We aim to monetize this outlet, publish books, produce screenplays, and release music.</p> <p>Plus, our partner organizations</p> <p><strong><a href="https://www.thelightphone.com/">Lightphone</a><br></strong><strong><a href="https://www.mill.com/">Mill</a><br></strong><strong><a href="https://ingredient-ai.com/">IngredientAI</a></strong></p> <h2>⛰️ The Head of Technology Role</h2> <p>The garden3d Head of Technology has one mandate: everything we build works, holds up in production, and gets built the smartest way available to us. We are a house of brands - Sanctuary Computer (development), XXIX (design), Index Space (community), USB Club (digital community), and the garden3d umbrella itself - and a lot of what all of them ship runs on software we wrote. Working in close partnership with our founder &amp; president Hugh Francis, this person sets the engineering standard, and builds the culture that holds it.</p> <p>You can be based anywhere. A lot of our people are in New York and there's some gravity here, but we already work across timezones and we would happily hire in Europe, Singapore, Chicago, or wherever you are. If you're the right person, we want to hear from you.</p> <p>This role works with studio leads, developers, designers, project managers and clients across every garden3d vertical.</p> <p>This person can move between a Rails migration, a Next.js app, a firmware release plan and an agent loop in the same week, and raise the bar on each of them.</p> <p>They span all of garden3d, but their home base is Sanctuary Computer, where roughly 70% of their time goes. Our development studio is where the engineering standard gets set, and where it either holds or slips: architecture, code review, estimation, and the hardest technical calls on our biggest projects. The other 30% goes to garden3d's broader technology story: how we ship product for USB Club, build with agents across the collective, which tools and platforms we bet on, and what we build for ourselves.</p> <p>They are also how we get better people. Our work is only as good as the engineers making it, so this person hunts for exceptional talent, sells them on us, and sets them up to do the best work of their careers. The ideal candidate looks at a worker-owned collective with four studios, an open P&amp;L and clients like Google, Stripe, Brooklyn Museum and The Nobel Prize, and sees an engineering practice they can propel among the best in the world.</p> <h2><strong>Responsibilities &amp; Mandates</strong></h2> <h3>️ <strong>Systems that hold up</strong></h3> <p>We build web apps, native apps, data pipelines, content platforms and connected devices for clients who can't afford for them to fall over. This person has engineered complex systems for a long time, and it shows in the architecture they draw before a line is written. They own the technical blueprint on our most important projects, and they make the hard calls on the rest: what to build, what to buy, and what to leave out.</p> <h3> <strong>All in on agentic development</strong></h3> <p>The way software gets built changed, and we intend to be ahead of it. This person is already deep in it: loop engineering, agents running against evals, agents that open their own PRs, and the guardrails that make all of that trustworthy. They make agentic development the default way Sanctuary Computer works, and they can tell the difference between a demo and a system a team can rely on.</p> <h3> <strong>Practical engineering</strong></h3> <p>We strongly prefer convention over configuration, boring technology, and platforms that let a small team ship a lot. TypeScript is the default language, Rails and Phoenix handle what they're best at, and we'd rather deploy to a platform like Render or Heroku than run our own infrastructure. This person practices value eng

oldContent: Crunchbase News https://news.crunchbase.com/ Data-driven reporting on private markets, startups, founders, and investors Thu, 15 Oct 2026 17:19:55 +0000 en-US hourly 1 https://wordpress.org/?v=6.8.11 https://news.crunchbase.com/wp-content/uploads/cb_news_favicon-150x150.png Crunchbase News https://news.crunchbase.com/ 32 32 Asia’s Startup Funding At Near Record High In Q3, Driven By AI https://news.crunchbase.com/venture/q3-2026-asia-startup-funding-near-record-ai/ Fri, 16 Oct 2026 11:00:42 +0000 https://news.crunchbase.com/?p=94235 Asia’s startup funding held up at the second-highest level in years in the third quarter, even as investment fell slightly from Q2 totals. Overall, investors put $38.5 billion into reported seed- through growth-stage financings for countries in the region in Q3, per Crunchbase data. Of that, a majority went to AI-focused companies, echoing the trends we’ve seen globally . Deal counts, meanwhile, were relatively flat. That indicates concentration of capital into favored startups remains pronounced but is not intensifying. Table of contents An AI-driven quarter China leads by far in country-by-country breakdown Late stage Early stage Seed A big quarter for China Methodology Glossary of funding terms An AI-driven quarter Around 55% of investment — an estimated $21 billion — went to AI-focused companies. Total funding is down substantially from the prior quarter, which was boosted by a $7.4 billion financing for China’s DeepSeek , but still the second-highest tally on record. For Q3, a couple of extra-large rounds bolstered the AI investment tally. The largest went to Beijing-based foundational model company Moonshot AI , which secured $3.5 billion in July at a reported $35 billion valuation. Kling AI , the AI spinout of China-based short video platform Kuaishou Technology , was the second-biggest fundraiser. The generative video startup raised around $3 billion in a July financing that included Baidu and Tencent . China leads by far in country-by-country breakdown China was the leading Asian destination for venture investment by a very wide margin. Per Crunchbase data, roughly $27 billion — or 70% of all Asian startup funding in Q3 — went to China-based companies. India was a distant second, with $2.9 billion, followed by Singapore, with $2.5 billion. For perspective, below we charted third-quarter startup funding tallies for the six countries with the largest totals. Late stage Most capital went to late- and growth-stage funding rounds. Per Crunchbase data, investment at this stage totaled around $20 billion in Q3. That’s down a bit from the prior quarter but nearly double year-ago levels and the second-strongest showing in four years. Multiple jumbo rounds kept the total high. The largest was Moonshot AI’s aforementioned $3.5 billion Series F. Several others raised financings in the multiple hundreds of millions. Shenzhen-based D-Robotics , a provider of robotics hardware and software, for instance, picked up $400 million in a September Series C. And Hong Kong-based Qupital , an e-commerce fintech platform, secured $300 million in Series C funding as it eyes an IPO. Early stage Early-stage investment drifted lower in Q3 but remained at historically high levels. Per Crunchbase data, financing for startups at the Series A and Series B stages totaled $13.6 billion for the just-ended quarter. That’s a decline of 28% from the prior quarter but up 65% from year-ago levels. Seed Reported seed funding hit its highest level in years, boosted by investor enthusiasm around AI. In total, investors poured $4.9 billion into reported seed and angel deals across Asia, per Crunchbase data. That’s up around 22% from the prior quarter and more than double year-ago levels. A big quarter for China Overall, Q3 was a robust period for venture funding to China-based companies, with far smaller sums going to other Asian startup hubs. Funding to startups based in India and Singapore was down significantly quarter over quarter, while Israel’s investment totals declined slightly. We’ll keep an eye out in the coming months to see if this divergence of fortunes persists. Check out The Crunchbase Megadeals Board . This is a weekly feature that runs down the week’s Top 10 announced funding rounds in the U.S. Check out last week’s biggest funding deal roundup here . Startup investors aren’t exactly hitting pause, but they did scale back on giant rounds this past week, with just two startup financings in the multiple hundreds of millions. The biggest round went to AI infrastructure provider Modal Labs , which picked up $750 million, followed by construction automation unicorn Icon , which secured $200 million. Other sectors that attracted larger rounds this past week included biotech, insurance and AI. 1. Modal Labs , $750M, AI infrastructure: Modal Labs, a provider of cloud infrastructure for AI inference and other applications, secured $750 million in a Series D funding round led by Accel at a $15.75 billion valuation. The New York-headquartered company said it recently exceeded an annual revenue run rate of $1 billion. 2. Icon , $200M, construction tech: Austin-based Icon, a developer of robotic construction systems known for its 3D-printed homes, closed on $200 million in Series D funding led by Baillie Gifford and BlackRock . The company says it is on pace for 4x revenue growth in 2026. 3. Soufflé Therapeutics , $135M, RNA therapies: Boston-based Soufflé Therapeutics, a developer of RNA therapies, raised $135 million in Series B funding led by Juvia Group as part of a large syndicate of investors. 4. Estuary Biotherapeutics , $103M, gene therapies: Menlo Park, California-based Estuary Biotherapeutics, a developer of genetic medicines for patients with serious kidney diseases, launched with $103 million in financing. The funding includes $93 million in a Series A round led by RA Capital Management as well as $10 million in previously undisclosed seed capital. 5. Labelbox , $100M, AI tools: Labelbox, a developer of technology to train and evaluate AI models and to help deploy agents that improve with experience, picked up $100 million in Series E funding. Infinitum Partners led the financing for the 8-year-old, San Francisco-based company. 6. Suki , $90M, health AI: Redwood City, California-based Suki, a provider of AI tools that turn clinical conversations into intelligence for documentation, coding and other healthcare workflows, announced a $90 million Series E financing from backers including Healthier Capital and Crosslink Capital . 7. Abby Care , $82M, caregiver platform: Abby Care, a platform for family members to become certified, paid caregivers and deliver care at home, closed on $82 million in Series C funding, per a Fortune report . Transformation Capital led the financing for the 5-year-old, San Francisco-based startup. 8. Stand , $70M, insurance: Stand, a provider of insurance for homes in areas at higher risk of natural disasters, secured $70 million in Series C funding at a $1 billion valuation. Saga Ventures led the financing for the 3-year-old, San Francisco-based company. 9. Mueon , $65M, semiconductor systems: Mueon Corp., a semiconductor systems company building a modular platform for AI and hyperscale computing, completed a $65 million Series A funding round. Maverick Silicon led the financing for the Portland, Oregon-based company. 10. North.cloud , $60M, AI spend management: New York-based North.cloud, provider of an infrastructure spend intelligence and automation platform, raised $60 million in a Series B round led by PeakSpan Capital . Methodology We tracked the largest announced rounds in the Crunchbase database that were raised by U.S.-based companies for the period of Oct. 10-16, 2026. Although most announced rounds are in the database, there may be a small time lag, as some rounds are reported late in the week.
